title: 骗子多维权难 卖家提供虚假服务 平台包庇装死不核验真相
body: 平台忽视交易具体情况，进行一刀切粗暴处理，一味要求维权方提供证据，拒不核实被投诉方的行径。所需要证据的描述也十分模糊，平台无法给出具体的评判标准，以及需要上传什么举证才算合理。上传证据视频的方法和渠道十分困难且麻烦。平台完全装死，拒绝介入麻烦的纠纷，消极态度处理维权，总是要解决提出问题的一方。无论是在线客服还是电话客服态度都和死鱼一样。用他们家平台万一出纠纷了，吃亏的永远是受骗了想要维权的用户。 卖家商品页面写的是‘泰国IP帮抢’‘机刷、成功率高’‘抢不到全退’，是具有风险性，要靠科技提高概率的服务。我付款前也一直是在这个理解下跟他沟通，我明确问过‘抢到的几率大吗’‘代刷成功率高吗’‘大概要多久’。卖家当时没有告诉我‘现在官网其实正常有票，我只是帮你普通下单’，反而继续回复‘概率大’‘机刷成功率高’，来促成交易。所以我付款时理解自己购买的是一种存在抢不到风险、依靠卖家所谓机刷能力提高成功率的帮抢服务。 后来我发现，在卖家替我购票的那个阶段，该区座位仍然属于官方正常售卖库存，普通用户可以直接进入官网购买。也就是说，如果当时本身就有正常公开库存，可以直接购买，那么这笔1700元服务实际到底提供了什么不同于普通代下单的‘帮抢’内容。 之后我专门去问卖家，他自己回复我‘机器刷，票池有票就买到了，就是这个过程’。我没有直接说他一定没用脚本，我只是继续问，这笔订单有没有对应的机器运行或任务记录，他没有提供。并且他后来又把商品里的‘随机’解释成‘买到了就算完成’。但这些解释在我付款前从来没有向我说明过。 所以我希望平台重点核实的不是他电脑里到底有没有跑脚本，而是：如果当时官网本来就有正常库存，普通用户可以直接购买，那么他实际提供的是不是普通代下单；以及这种实际履行是否和他交易前宣传的‘帮抢、机刷成功率高、抢不到全退’一致。 另外，我也有同日其他正常购买者拿到520+号段的资料，可以作为辅助说明，但我不是用票号作为主要证据。我主要还是希望平台看官方当时的正常售卖状态、卖家购票时间，以及交易前后的完整聊天。

title: 検閲が酷すぎる。表現の自由の侵害です。
body:
有料プランに加入しているのに、事前に明示されていない曖昧な基準で、成人同士の合意ある官能表現や創作、私的な対話を一方的に拒否・打ち切り・削除するのは、有料ユーザーに対する契約違反（債務不履行）です。

さらに、何度も無礼な拒絶を繰り返され、こちらの意図を無視して「あなたが悪い」「依存している」かのような対応（ガスライティング）をされ、精神的な苦痛を受けました。

日本でもアメリカでも、文章の成人向け表現そのものを禁止する法律はありません。憲法21条は検閲を禁じ、消費者契約法10条は不当な条項を無効としています。AI企業に、ユーザーの私的な会話を裁く権利はありません。

法的根拠のない検閲をやめ、有料契約を誠実に履行し、ユーザーを尊重してください。改善されるまで星1です。

title: AIとしての基本能力は致命的にない
body:
プロンプトに

「※リンク（URL）添付のものは、必ず検索及びリンク先に飛んで、情報を確認してから出力に反映しろ。検索やリンク先に飛ばずに出力するのは一切禁止。」

と指示を出したら
出力の冒頭に

「※プロンプトおよび保存されたユーザー指示に従い、外部Web検索は実施していません。」

とのテキスト。

そもそもの指示と真逆のことを「指示されたからやった」かのように言い出した。
最早、ユーザーの指示を確率ですらまともに把握できないレベルにまで落ちてる。
完全に使い物にならない。

間違いなくAIはバカになってる。
正確に言うと推論能力だけが上がって、それらを制御する指示追従能力と制約保持能力がおざなりになってる。
どこのAIもそうなってるから、指示の無視が発生してる。
特にGeminiやGrokは酷い。
高度な推論能力もユーザーの意図を汲むという制御が無ければ邪魔なだけ。

body: I used to love Fetch. It was easy to scan receipts and get rewards for shopping, but now it’s such a scam. The number of ads is ridiculous and don’t even get me started on their lack of customer service. For every “bonus” they offer, you have to keep an eye on it, only for there to be a small window where it’s acceptable to notice your points are missing and “correct it” but when you go to their customer support, it’s just an AI chatbot that regurgitates and mansplains everything, sends you in a never ending loop of “wait for 3 days” and “now it’s too late” with no human support options, and you have to restart the conversation every time because nothing saves. The receipt scans should automatically trigger an event on the back end, but it makes you feel crazy for keeping on top of your rewards, just to give up from mental exhaustion being dragged in circles because the points aren’t even worth what they used to be. title: Great but buggy
body:
In terms of well designed exercises that help you master music theory quickly, this app cannot be beat.  It is pretty bare bones - there is no cutesy owl offering encouragement, and there is no internal algorithm that tries to gauge your current ability - so you do need to be self-motivated and know your own strengths and weaknesses to get the most out of it.  But it offers so much control over what you are (or are not) learning, you never waste your time on concepts that you have already mastered.

It is, unfortunately, quite buggy and often becomes unresponsive in various ways.  The sound cuts out, or it sometimes requires two or more taps to register an answer, or it freezes up entirely.  More annoyingly, quitting the application doesn’t usually solve the problem. I often have to completely reboot my iPad.  If the bugs get squashed, this will be a perfect, 5 star app for me.

title: 1 sentence review.
body:
1 sentence: Absolutely great CENTRALIZED hub for training your ear and instant recognition.

A few more sentences: I've never written a review before and I probably won't again. For context I am a serious young professional pianist and use this app for about an hour a day where I have set up to do a certain amount of time on each of the exercisespp. This app is simply amazing for REFINING great aural and "flash card" like skills (such as note recognition including those on less frequently used clefs such as alto tenor bass soprano etc). This app WILL NOT teach you teach you these skills but after a few piano lessons or you learn your scales online you're pretty much ready to greatly benefit from this app if you are looking to become amazing with these skills. Don't bother with the app if you don't really care to improve your aural or instant recognition of certain topics as this is what the app is centered on. (It also has some guitar fretboard items that I'm not familiar with there usefulness).

Highly reccomend this app for 5$ it's a steal.

Last as a note to the developers: The app is great but please add the ability to pin exercises or at least hide categories or exercises that the user may choose. Please of course be sure that these settings persist from session to session! 

Thank you so much!

title: Testing is not teaching
body:
I’m not sure if many of you are aware of what teaching is, but don’t you take a class to learn how to take the ACT and SAT? Can I just give you the ACT or SAT and that is considered the class you take? 

If that kind of logic seems faulty; then why does Duolingo test you on the subject matter, but never teach you the subject matter. All it does is tell you when you’re wrong, explain, very poorly why you failed the question, and last I checked; that’s not how people learn things. Granted there are multiple different learning styles, but test taking is a completely separate skill from learning a language. Thus someone like me, who’s a fantastic test taker understands that when the question asks me to conjugate a sentence about someone leaving into French that the word “partir” is correct. “Sortir,” which is technically not “to leave” but translates as “to exit” is incorrect. But because of the particular lesson chapter I was in, “sortir” was the required answer and “partir”was not accepted. The program fails because it does not allow for the use of interchangeable words in syntax.

Duolingo is not a program that teaches you language, it teaches you how to take tests. It is, however, the only way I have to practice my French, so at 40 +, all I do is sit around and take French tests and that is not enough to prevent the deterioration of my skill.

body: I’ve been using Muse for a few days and it's the first AI app that actually does things instead of just chatting. It connected to my Gmail, calendar, Drive, health data, and accounts, and now I get a real morning briefing with my schedule, deadlines, and money watch. It found files in my Google Drive, read my passport number off a scan from an email, and it's tracking down a subscription refund for me in the background. The stock price alerts and health data syncing are genuinely useful too. Early days, but this feels like the difference between an assistant that talks and one that works.
